ledger.note: 1822: Moshoeshoe becomes the first king of the Basotho. 'He became the first and ultimately longest-serving King of Lesotho in 1822.' (In 1820 he 'succeeded his father as the Bamokoteli chief'.)

ledger.note: 19 March 1858: the Orange Free State declares war on the Basotho over the Caledon lands. 'Boshoff declaring war on the Basotho on 19 March 1858 (also reported as 22 March 1858).' The date is the declaration; the page gives no first-campaign date.

region.text: the 'Conquered Territory': the area 'between the Caledon and Orange rivers' fought over 'from present day Wepener to Zastron', which the 1869 convention 'gave ... to the Orange Free State'

ledger.note: 1 June 1858: an armistice ends the first war. 'On 1 June an armistice was agreed upon and signed, under which all military operations on both sides were to be suspended.' The page names no boundary.

ledger.note: 1865: the Free State launches the Seqiti War. 'In 1865, the Orange Free State launched the Second Basotho War known in Sesotho as the Seqiti War.' The page gives no month.

ledger.note: 11 April 1866: Moshoeshoe accepts the peace of Thaba Bosiu. 'compelled to accept the peace of Thaba Bosiu on 11 April 1866'; the Moshoeshoe page: he 'ceded most of his kingdom's arable land to the Boers'; the FSB page adds that he 'had not agreed to the frontier line of 1866'.

ledger.note: July 1867: the third war begins. 'In July 1867, the third war between the Orange Free State and the Basotho began.'

12 March 1868: Britain takes Moshoeshoe's people under its protection. 'On 12 March 1868, a proclamation declared the Basotho to be British subjects and Basutoland to be British territory.' The Free State-Basotho page calls it a protectorate and an annexation; the Basotho kingdom becomes 'Basutoland'.

notes: Cliopatria has no Basutoland: its Lesotho row (slug lesotho, written by af-08) begins in 1967; this dossier is the state before it, and the Cape Colony and Orange Free State dossiers (af-07-a and af-07-b) already cite it as counterpart 'basutoland'. Budget: Basutoland, Moshoeshoe I and Free State-Basotho Wars (three pages for a no-shape state; the Moshoeshoe page was thin on territory). Not on any page opened: the founding at Butha-Buthe, the move to Thaba Bosiu (1824), the Warden Line and Sovereignty (1848-49), the 1851 Viervoet and 1852 Berea battles beyond their dates, the 1869 treaty's name ('Convention of Aliwal North' per FSB), the Letsie rulers, the 1910 High Commission Territory status (mentioned, not dated to a boundary). The British protection of 1868-71 and the protectorate from 1884 to 1966 are British-side vassal events (counterpart basutoland, suzerain british-colonial-empire or british-cape-colony), which this ledger shows only as a rename (1868) and the Cape annexation (loss 1871, gain 1884). Region name 'Conquered Territory' is not yet in the gazetteer (the Free State dossier uses it too); the Free State is ordinary admin1. The Moshoeshoe page and the FSB page differ on the Treaty of Thaba Bosiu terms (arable land ceded vs no land specified): the ledger keeps the transfer at 1869. Sibling dossiers date the 1858 contest end to 15 October 1858 (their page); this ledger uses the 1 June armistice from the FSB page. REPAIR 2026-10-19 (after review): keyframe basutoland_1869 now ends in 1870 and basutoland_1884 (1884-1966) is added, so Lesotho is drawn by the Cape alone in 1871-1883 and not by two states. The dossier keeps its life (1822-1966) and its colour through the gap because the same colony is re-established under the same name in 1884 (rule 2); the Gun War contest (1880-1881, Lesotho against the Cape) is unchanged. The alternative the reviewer offered (a vassal relation with the Cape matching in the Cape dossier) was not taken: the page says the territory was 'annexed' by an Act of the Cape Parliament, not that it was a vassal.
